header: Date: 2027-02-14 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Vega (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Redwood Product), Lena Ortiz (Kestrel Head of Data Privacy), Samir Patel (Kestrel Platform), Olivia Reed (Kestrel Security), Tomás Delgado (ML)
summary: Redwood team demoed request storage toggles, redaction flow, ephemeral vs persisted request lifecycle, and integration points for KMS and SSO. Customer wants pilot to validate retention-ejection behavior and confirm audit log fidelity for compliance. Action: send security docs, console video, and set pilot with Dedicated cluster.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um — quick intros then we'll jump into the console tour. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account.
[00:00:18] Lena (Kestrel): Hi, Lena here. We're the privacy owner, mostly interested in how request storage and redaction will look operationally.
[00:00:27] Carlos (Redwood SE): Hi, Carlos — I'll lead the demo. We'll show API + Console flows, and also the Optimize suggestions for retention.
[00:00:40] Samir (Kestrel): Samir, platform eng. Quick note, our primary constraint is EU-only data residency and we need to tie into our cloud KMS.
[00:00:52] Maya (Redwood AE): Great, that's helpful, we'll point out the KMS/HSM integration and RBAC hooks.
[00:01:05] Carlos (Redwood SE): Ok jumping into the Console. First screen is request storage — by default it's "persist" for troubleshooting but you can toggle to "ephemeral" or "persist with redaction". The toggle also shows retention schedule and ejection policy.
[00:01:30] [00:01:30] Carlos (Redwood SE): Notice here we've got a lifecycle timeline: ingest -> short-term cache -> persisted store -> ejection. You can set policies per-route or per-model.
[00:01:58] Tomás (Kestrel): Is the persisted store encrypted at rest, and can we use our KMS keys?
[00:02:10] Carlos (Redwood SE): Yes, data at rest is encrypted; we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. You can bring keys from AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or customer HSM through our Private deployment.
[00:02:34] Olivia (Kestrel): From a compliance view we need the audit logs to show exactly when PII was redacted — is that included?
[00:02:47] Carlos (Redwood SE): Good question. Audit logs capture the retention policy change, redaction events (with non-sensitive metadata), and ejection timestamps. We don't store original PII in the audit event; it's a pointer.
[00:03:05] Lena (Kestrel): When you say redaction events, is that automatic pattern-based redaction or is it deferred so we can run custom scrubbers?
[00:03:18] Carlos (Redwood SE): Both. We have built-in pattern and ML-based PII detectors — email, ssn-like patterns, passports — and you can also plug in a webhook for deferred redaction or a Lambda to run custom logic before persisting. We call it deferred scrub.
[00:03:46] [00:03:46] Maya (Redwood AE): For your use case, many customers do client-side hashing for identifiers plus server-side redaction to reduce exposure.
[00:04:05] Samir (Kestrel): Would client-side hashing break our ability to debug prompts during pilot?
[00:04:18] Carlos (Redwood SE): It reduces fidelity but you can run a short-lived debug mode where request storage is persisted for a narrow window, then auto-ejected. There is also token-level cost/latency breakdowns so you can see what's happening without storing raw PII.
[00:04:44] Tomás (Kestrel): How configurable is the retention window? For us it needs to be 7 days max for non-PII and 0 days for identified PII if possible.
[00:04:58] Carlos (Redwood SE): Policies are per-route. You can set retention to 0d, 7d, 30d etc, and have conditional rules: if PII detected then immediate ejection or move to ephemeral. There's also a 'quarantine' tier — requests stay encrypted and inaccessible pending manual review.
[00:05:25] [00:05:25] Lena (Kestrel): Quarantine sounds useful, what's the manual review workflow?
[00:05:36] Carlos (Redwood SE): Quarantine notifies your Data Steward via webhook/SMS/SLACK integration, and you can approve a time-limited reveal. Everything is audited and we surface the redaction rationale in the console.
[00:05:58] Samir (Kestrel): We need to ensure ejection actually removes data from all caches — including K V cache — not just the persisted blob.
[00:06:12] Carlos (Redwood SE): Yes, we have a KV cache flush on ejection and we purge local GPU-hosted caches. In Dedicated mode you can also schedule rolling cache wipes.
[00:06:32] [00:06:32] Maya (Redwood AE): Quick interjection — a common ask: how does this change our SLA during a spike? There was concern about latency vs cost tradeoff with persistent debugging enabled.
[00:06:45] Tomás (Kestrel): Exactly — we can't afford consistent tail-latencies.
[00:06:52] Carlos (Redwood SE): For spikes we recommend an autoscale policy that routes to a lower-cost variant for non-critical routes and preserves high-perf instances for low-latency routes. Also ephemeral mode helps — no disk I/O for persisting requests so it improves tail latency.
[00:07:22] [00:07:22] Olivia (Kestrel): Is there a way to mask PII in the transcript while still preserving some tokens for model context?
[00:07:34] Carlos (Redwood SE): Yes, selective token masking keeps structural tokens but replaces sensitive spans with deterministic placeholders, e.g., <EMAIL_HASH:abcd>. You can configure the hashing algorithm (sha256/sha1) and whether it's reversible with a key.
[00:07:58] Lena (Kestrel): Reversible with a key worries me. We prefer non-reversible by default.
[00:08:07] Carlos (Redwood SE): Default is non-reversible. Reversible placeholders require explicit KMS operations and strong audit trails.
[00:08:19] [00:08:19] Maya (Redwood AE): Quick glance at Optimize — this shows recommendations like batch sizes, cache TTLs, and quantization level to hit your cost target while keeping latency SLOs. It also recommends storage class changes when we detect low access patterns.
[00:08:43] Tomás (Kestrel): Can Optimize suggest retention windows? That would be helpful to balance debugability vs compliance.
[00:08:53] Carlos (Redwood SE): Yes, Optimize can suggest retention policies based on request frequency and whether PII is commonly detected. It's a heuristic, you can accept or tune it.
[00:09:10] [00:09:10] Lena (Kestrel): Let's talk about audit log retention for compliance — we have to retain non-sensitive audit trails for 3 years.
[00:09:22] Carlos (Redwood SE): Audit logs are separate from request storage and we have retention tiers up to multi-year. For compliance you can export logs to your SIEM or a secure bucket, and we can also sign log envelopes for tamper evidence.
[00:09:45] Samir (Kestrel): Exporting to our SIEM is a hard requirement. Does that require Private deployment?
[00:09:56] Carlos (Redwood SE): No, hosted supports secure log export over private peering or VPC egress; for strict network isolation you can opt for Private or Dedicated.
[00:10:15] [00:10:15] Maya (Redwood AE): We're about halfway through — any blockers so far?
[00:10:22] Lena (Kestrel): I want to see the exact redaction logs format.
[00:10:28] Carlos (Redwood SE): We'll attach a sample JSON schema after the call. It includes event id, timestamp, policy id, redaction reason, and non-sensitive hash.
[00:10:45] [00:10:45] Tomás (Kestrel): For the pilot, we'd like to run a small batch of prompts through your API to validate ejection behavior. What's the best way?
[00:10:56] Carlos (Redwood SE): We'll spin up a Dedicated pilot slice for you — small GPU pool — and you can hit the API endpoints. We'll preconfigure retention rules and KMS. We can also provide a script to replay sanitized production traffic.
[00:11:30] [00:11:30] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll need an NDA addendum for access to sanitized logs during the pilot, Maya (note: she said Maya twice) — sorry, I meant we'll route NDA request to you folks.
[00:11:50] Lena (Kestrel): Good. Also how do we handle legal data subject requests? Can we programmatically query by user id and eject all related requests?
[00:12:03] Carlos (Redwood SE): Yes, we support DSR workflows: query by fingerprint or pseudonym, then either redact or eject. There's a dry-run mode to see how many records match before action.
[00:12:22] [00:12:22] Olivia (Kestrel): Is there any risk of partial deletion leaving traces in model weight caches?
[00:12:33] Carlos (Redwood SE): We do not modify model weights. The risk is transient in KV caches, which we flush on ejection. For absolute guarantees, we provide a forced cache invalidate and rotation.
[00:12:58] [00:12:58] Samir (Kestrel): How are these operations logged for auditors? Can we provide a signed timeline?
[00:13:08] Carlos (Redwood SE): Yes, we can produce signed audit envelopes and chain-of-custody artifacts. We also integrate with your SIEM to ship raw events.
[00:13:30] [00:13:30] Maya (Redwood AE): I'll pause demo and show the API flow. The /v1/requests endpoint includes a header to indicate storage policy (X-Redwood-Retention: ephemeral|persist|redact).
[00:13:52] Tomás (Kestrel): If we miss the header, can server-side default policies trigger?
[00:14:01] Carlos (Redwood SE): Yes, server-side policy is applied by route. Header overrides are allowed if authorized by role.
[00:14:20] [00:14:20] Carlos (Redwood SE): There's also a batch endpoint for bulk ejections and a status API for job progress. The status API reports counts, matching reason codes.
[00:14:38] Lena (Kestrel): Can we restrict who can call the status API?
[00:14:44] Carlos (Redwood SE): RBAC controls allow scoping by role and by IP. We also support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning.
[00:15:05] [00:15:05] Samir (Kestrel): We use Okta — so SAML + SCIM is important for us.
[00:15:12] Maya (Redwood AE): Ok noted. Next I'll walkthrough a quick what-if: you have a customer support tool that sends unsanitized transcripts; how do you minimize exposure?
[00:15:31] Carlos (Redwood SE): Route that traffic to a separate tenant or route with strict retention=0 and client-side hashing; also set a temporary debug window if needed.
[00:15:50] [00:15:50] Tomás (Kestrel): Do you support client libraries that do pre-send redaction?
[00:15:57] Carlos (Redwood SE): We provide SDK hooks and sample scrubbers for Node/Python, plus a small WASM sanitizer for browser flows.
[00:16:20] [00:16:20] Maya (Redwood AE): Alright, we pulled up a compliance playbook — it's a shared doc which lists policy templates for legal/DSR, KMS integration steps, and a pilot checklist.
[00:16:36] Lena (Kestrel): Can we see the playbook?
[00:16:40] Maya (Redwood AE): Yes we'll share after. Link is in the chat (https://redwood.ai/privacy-playbook).
[00:16:55] [00:16:55] Olivia (Kestrel): On the redaction ML detector — what's the false positive rate and can we tune sensitivity?
[00:17:07] Carlos (Redwood SE): Current detector is tuned to conservative recall; you can tune sensitivity per-route and supply custom regex lists. For pilot we'll provide metrics from similar customers.
[00:17:30] Tomás (Kestrel): For performance testing, can we run synthetic traffic with PII patterns to validate detection latency impact?
[00:17:40] Carlos (Redwood SE): Absolutely, we'll include a synthetic generator and a replay tool to measure CPU/GPU impact.
[00:18:03] [00:18:03] Maya (Redwood AE): Quick note — some customers choose to tokenize sensitive spans before sending to Redwood so the service sees only tokens. That reduces liability.
[00:18:22] Lena (Kestrel): We'll consider tokenization, but it adds dev work.
[00:18:29] [00:18:29] Carlos (Redwood SE): One more thing: for long-term archival, we recommend exporting minimal audit envelopes to your secure bucket with pointer references back to ephemeral ids, not the raw text.
[00:18:49] Samir (Kestrel): How does billing work for persisted vs ephemeral?
[00:18:59] Maya (Redwood AE): Persisted request storage may add a small per-request storage charge and retrieval; We'll provide an example cost sheet. During pilot costs are usually absorbed in the pilot pricing.
[00:19:18] [00:19:18] Tomás (Kestrel): Any limitations around private deployments and the retention features?
[00:19:30] Carlos (Redwood SE): Private supports all retention features and gives you local network control; Dedicated gives predictable throughput but hosted is fastest for time-to-value.
[00:19:55] [00:19:55] Lena (Kestrel): Let's surface the privacy playbook items we need: encryption keys, DSR flow, audit export, sample redaction logs.
[00:20:08] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll compile those and send them.
[00:20:16] [00:20:16] Carlos (Redwood SE): Ok wrapping up demo — any final technical concerns?
[00:20:22] Olivia (Kestrel): Need to confirm our SIEM schema mapping.
[00:20:28] Samir (Kestrel): Also want to validate ejection actually removes artifacts from GPU / host temp files.
[00:20:34] Carlos (Redwood SE): We'll include a checklist for ejection verification and a script to run during pilot.
[00:20:48] [00:20:48] Maya (Redwood AE): Great. For next steps: we'll send security docs, schedule Dedicated pilot, and share console video.
[00:20:58] Lena (Kestrel): Sounds good. If possible, have the pilot include EU region-only infra.
[00:21:07] Carlos (Redwood SE): No problem, EU-only Dedicated slice.
[00:21:16] [00:21:16] Tomás (Kestrel): Timeline — we can start the pilot next Monday if we get the paperwork.
[00:21:23] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll target next Monday, will circulate dates later today.
[00:21:30] [00:21:30] Maya (Redwood AE): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email with artifacts.
[00:21:40] [00:21:40] Lena (Kestrel): Thanks all.
[00:21:45] [00:21:45] Speaker 6: (garbled) mhm thanks bye
[00:21:50] [00:21:50] END: Brief final notes: promised items — console video, SOC2 doc, ejection verification script.

Note: transcription has occasional speaker overlaps and small recognition errors (e.g., K V cache for KV cache, SAMEL for SAML in one auto-sentence).
